overall: Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an April 19 notice with insufficient topic detail (executive session and several open session topics); other allegations were rejected or declined.

allegations.summary: Board entered executive session for an improper purpose, namely contract negotiations with the Town Manager, which the complaint said was not a proper basis for closed session.
allegations.key_passage: We conclude, however, that the discussions in executive session, which pertained to contract negotiations, fell within a proper statutory purpose.

allegations.summary: Executive session topic on the April 19 notice did not name the Town Manager as the nonunion personnel being negotiated with, so the topic lacked sufficient detail.
allegations.key_passage: we conclude that the topic as listed on the original notice should have included the Town Manager as the Board does not suggest that inclusion of such information would have compromised the purpose for the executive session.

allegations.summary: Board refused to let the public into the meeting when the chair told a member of the public he needed to leave before the executive session vote.
allegations.key_passage: we do not believe the Board intentionally excluded the complainant or any other member of the public from this portion of the meeting.

allegations.summary: Notice failed to identify an open session portion of the meeting in addition to the anticipated executive session.
allegations.key_passage: In addition, it was clear that an open session meeting would take place as the full notice included additional open session topics.

allegations.summary: Several open session topics ('Vicious Dog Hearing', 'IMA with Hopkinton', 'Aggregation', Kid Spot appointments) were too vague on the 48-hour notice; revisions within 48 hours did not cure them.
allegations.key_passage: However, we find that certain other topics were not sufficiently detailed, including "Vicious Dog Hearing" which should have included an address, "IMA with Hopkinton" which contained an acronym not widely understood by members of the public, and "Aggregation" which was not adequately defined.

allegations.summary: Board conducted the Town Manager's performance evaluation outside a properly posted meeting, through individual evaluation forms compiled by the chair and a statement read at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Board followed this directive when the members submitted their individual evaluations of the Town Manager to Chair Magnani.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly told the complainant to 'just file another complaint'.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law and we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to provide a copy of open session minutes from the April 19 meeting, a claim not raised in the original complaint to the Board.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation as well because, after a careful review, we find that it was not included within the April 19 complaint to the Board and the Board has not had an opportunity to respond to it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements (notice content / topic specificity).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
